newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran says German envoy not welcome for now.
newsitem.headline: Iran says German envoy not welcome for now.

text.p: Iran's spiritual leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei on Wednesday ordered the Foreign Ministry not to allow the German ambassador to return to Tehran for now or to send back Iranian envoys to European states, the official news agency IRNA said.

"The supreme leader ordered the Iranian Foreign Ministry not to allow the German ambassador to Tehran to return for a period of time. The leader also instructed the Foreign Ministry not to rush in sending back Iranian ambassadors to their respective missions in the EU member states," it said.
Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati was also quoted as saying Tehran "will not be upset if the German ambassador never returns to Tehran and we may even be...pleased."

EU foreign ministers on Tuesday announced they were suspending ministerial ties with Iran over an April 10 German court verdict accusing Iranian leaders of ordering political killings in Berlin in 1992.
They said ambassadors could return to Tehran if their governments wished. Only Greece of the 15 EU member states had not recalled its envoy from the Iranian capital after the court ruling.
Iran -- which denied any links to the Berlin killings -- retaliated by recalling its envoys from Europe.
Khamenei described Western governments as "unfair, ill-intentioned, shameless and brazen because of their baseless accusations against the Iranian nation and other nations of the world."

Iran's President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani also on Wednesday accused the EU states of indulging in "childish games" and said Tehran had halted "critical dialogue" with Europe prior to a similar European move.

"Critical dialogue, the suspension of which is being hailed as an achievement by Europeans, had been suspended before this at the instigation of Iran," IRNA quoted Rafsanjani as telling an energy conference in Iran. He did not elaborate.
The EU had said it suspended its policy of critical dialogue -- which involved talks with Tehran while trying to get Iran to move closer to the West -- following the court verdict.
Iran's Foreign Ministry in a statement carried by IRNA earlier on Wednesday slammed as invalid Tuesday's EU decisions, which it said was a grave breach of international law.
